text.tspan: Bytes are proxied through the backend. audio.audioFileUrl and the S3 key derived from it stay server-side. No S3 URL and no presigned link ever reaches the browser.

g.text: [authenticated route, /api/** is .authenticated() so JWTAuthenticationFilter must have populated the context]

text.tspan: Content-Disposition: inline, sanitised ASCII filename plus RFC 5987 filename* for Kurdish and Arabic titles
Cache-Control: public, max-age=300 on the guest route, no-store, private on the authenticated one
Send no Range header at all and the same method returns 200 OK with the whole object and no Content-Range. The 206 is chosen
solely by isRangeRequest, not by the size served.
Real cost. Every stream call makes exactly two S3 round trips: one HeadObject for the total size, then one ranged GetObject. Nothing is cached,
so each seek pays both again.
There is no 416 branch. parseRange clamps a malformed or unsatisfiable header instead of rejecting it, so Range: bytes=9000000- on this object
returns start = end = 9000000, S3 answers 416, and mapStorageError only special-cases statusCode 404 — the browser is handed a 500.
AudioStreamAPI caps nothing. readAllBytes buffers the whole requested window on the heap, so bytes=0- or a Range-less request pulls the entire
object into memory. VideoStreamAPI avoids that with its 2 MiB first window.

svg.text: key parsed out of the URL path, no S3 call made here
stream, closed by the try-with-resources in downloadRange
mapStorageError gives 404 NOT_FOUND when the cause is an S3Exception with statusCode 404, else 500 Failed to stream
